scope: AMH sex comparison in minipuberty only; no changes to source profiles, ordinary lifespan views, puberty comparison or laboratory reference intervals.
sourceFilesPolicy: Complete articles and original female supplement were inspected. No full PDFs, figures, participant data or local file paths are redistributed.

sources.location: Figure 3, p 1565; hormone assays, Methods p 1561
sources.population: 119 healthy term singleton Caucasian boys followed postnatally; COPENHAGEN Minipuberty Study, Denmark, 2016–2018; 338 postnatal serum samples. Total paper population 128 includes 9 cord-only boys.
sources.assay: Beckman Coulter Access 2 chemiluminescence, B13127, RRID AB_2892998
sources.statistic: Age-specific GAMLSS median, approximate vector-PDF extraction; not Figure 2 normalized longitudinal mean.
sources.caution: Stored decimal precision exceeds the source figure resolution. The paper’s longitudinal mean AMH peak at 146 days is another statistic, not a replacement for this median maximum.

sources.population: 98 healthy term singleton Caucasian girls; COPENHAGEN Minipuberty Study, Denmark; 266 serum samples, median 3 per girl (IQR 1–4), observed from 5 days to 14.2 months.
sources.assay: Beckman Coulter Access 2 chemiluminescence, RRID AB_2892998
sources.statistic: Age-specific GAMLSS median from original supplement Table D, not the biphasic normalized longitudinal mean trajectory.

supplement.table: D; median column, selected ages 0.02–1 years
supplement.independentTranscription: All 99 current AMH median values exactly match the original table. Original supplement has 121 rows, age 0–1.2 years; this change does not enlarge the active subset.

sources.caution: LOQ 2.9 and 4.0 pmol/L in the assay paragraph belong to estrone and estradiol, not AMH. The model median has one broad maximum; do not import two peaks from the separately modelled mean trajectory.

fixedScale.meaning: Equal heights mean equal concentrations. One tick step is a tenfold ratio, not an equal additive difference. Limits are graphical boundaries, not normal limits or assay detection bounds.

presentation.curves: Sample the same two unchanged source profiles through referenceAt, independently of patient or result; no separate normalization and no Wang substitution at age 1.
presentation.reproduction: VildaHormoneLifespanDisplay.buildAmhInfantComparison(data, referenceEngine); source checkpoints: referenceEngine.referenceAt(profile, ageDays/365.25) * 0.1401. Data: vilda_hormone_lifespan_data.js; engine: vilda_hormone_lifespan_reference.js.

approvedSampleCheck.meaning: All 2057 approved preview samples matched the actual source engine. This is technical reproducibility, not independent clinical validation.

presentation.referencePolicy: The original evaluate function qualifies the point, including the whole age interval, term birth, method, specimen, unit and uncensored finite nonnegative value. Existing profiles and source-domain boundaries stay unchanged.
edgeCases: Male age 7–<7.305 days may retain his own source reference and point before shared curve support. No female curve is extrapolated to this interval.
Exactly 1 year has no patient point in this paired infant view for either sex. The female source endpoint remains valid in its original profile elsewhere; male Wang remains available in other views.
Preterm or unknown birth status does not qualify for either term-infant point, but does not change or remove these educational population curves. Do not substitute corrected age.
Exact numeric 0 or a result below 0.1 ng/mL: below-axis arrow and unchanged value, no log(0), artificial positive floor or fabricated precise dot. Above 1000: above-axis arrow and unchanged value.
A result with < or > is not an exact point. Do not replace censored measurements with the source modelling convention LOD/2.
Floating-point tolerance at an axis edge only prevents SI roundtrip artifacts, e.g. 1000.0000000000001 ng/mL; it is not assay or clinical tolerance.
presentation.assayFloor: LOD 0.14 pmol/L ≈0.019614 ng/mL is below the chosen display floor. All existing median values exceed 0.1 ng/mL. The axis floor is not the LOD; no AMH-specific LOQ was reported.

checkpointQualification: Numeric entries are source-engine checkpoints, including interpolation between female table knots; they do not create norms. At 365.25 days male Busch is null, female source remains 0.9916278 ng/mL, but neither patient point is shown in this comparison. The male left limit is ≈166.471455 ng/mL.
limitations: Same method and study setting support descriptive sex comparison, not assay-independent diagnostic limits.
Cohort medians do not show individual variability or the course of a particular child; model-specific peak timing is not an exact individual event.
The male graph read and female rounded table/interpolation have different numerical precision.
Both cohorts concern healthy term singletons and are not preterm references.
No new laboratory norm, threshold, percentile, SDS, diagnosis or treatment recommendation follows from a point’s distance to a median.
